## Summary

- The Console manages User Groups and Subject Attributes. A User Group is a named set of Users and carries no permissions of its own. A Subject Attribute is a typed value on a User or a User Group that an Entity row rule can compare.
- Entity Access Control decides which rows and attributes a person can read or write. A grant names one subject: a User, a Role, or a User Group. Presentation ladders, access profiles, grants, and restrictions are the policy.
- For each existing published Entity, upgrade seeds an `all_clear` profile and one grant per Role that already has entity data permissions, so current readers keep access. Profile views for that seed are built by a worker job, not during the migration.
- A deprecated Business Entity is closed.
- New installs persist Postgres on the named volume `refraq_pg` at `/var/lib/postgresql`. A site already mounted there keeps its cluster. A site installed only from the v0.1.8 asset must move the anonymous-volume cluster onto that named volume before `up -d`.

## Operator notes

- Add `ENTITY_OWNER_PASSWORD` and `ENTITY_READER_PASSWORD` to the live `.env` before `docker compose up`. Both are required, URL-safe, and distinct from each other. If either is unset, Compose aborts interpolation and containers that are already running stay up.
- Back up Postgres before upgrading.
- Postgres data for this compose is the image volume `/var/lib/postgresql` on the named volume `refraq_pg`. Default PGDATA is `/var/lib/postgresql/18/docker`. `/var/lib/postgresql/data` is not the data directory. A site already mounted at `/var/lib/postgresql`, including one hand-edited to that path, keeps its data when this compose replaces the site file, provided `refraq_pg` already contains the cluster.
- A site that only ever used the published v0.1.8 asset (`refraq_pg:/var/lib/postgresql/data`) has the cluster on an anonymous volume at `/var/lib/postgresql/18/docker`. Replacing compose and running `up -d` without moving that cluster initdb's an empty cluster on `refraq_pg`. Before `up -d`, while the v0.1.8 compose is still in place, stop postgres without removing volumes (`docker compose stop postgres`). Copy the anonymous volume's `18` directory onto the named volume through that container's mounts: `docker run --rm --entrypoint cp --volumes-from "$(docker compose ps -aq postgres)" pgvector/pgvector:pg18 -a /var/lib/postgresql/18 /var/lib/postgresql/data/18`. After the new mount, the cluster is at `/var/lib/postgresql/18/docker`. Or dump with `pg_dumpall` as `refraq` and restore after the new cluster is up. There is no automatic copy.
- Replace `docker-compose.yaml`, then `docker compose pull && docker compose up -d` only after that move, or immediately when the site is already mounted at `/var/lib/postgresql` or is a new install.
- `ensure-entity-db` runs the entity bootstrap. It moves Entity Tables whose names end in `__v<digits>__` plus 16 hex digits, and stem views that read only those tables, from `public` into `entity_data`, and enables and forces row level security on those tables.
- API start runs Foundation Upgrade, including metadata revisions `0050_entity_attribute_ids` through `0054_entity_access_seed`. The seed does not build profile views. Entity data requests can answer `503 ENTITY_ACCESS_PENDING` until the worker finishes the view job.
- Rolling back to an older compose after this bootstrap and these migrations is not supported.
